normalized.governing_thought: Yes, raise prices in 2027 by segment: +10% for mid-market and enterprise, hold SMB until a test reads out, and retain the promo cohort without a price rise
executive_summary: Answer: The recommended plan adds about $3.0M of net ARR in 2027, and up to $0.5M more if the SMB test passes. It gives the same ~$2.0M as the CFO's flat +12% in the downside case and less SMB risk. No pricing option reaches the 15% growth target on its own; new customers must supply the last ~$1.9M.

1. Churn is rising because of one cohort, not because customers broadly reject the price. Core SMB churn went from 2.0% to only 2.1% a month. The 2,100 customers from the 2025 promotion churn at ~4.9% a month and make up 56% of SMB churners. Better onboarding explains only ~30% of their excess churn; the rest is a reaction to the discount ending.

2. Mid-market and enterprise can take a price rise; SMB has not shown it can. Mid-market: a +10% test had no significant effect on conversion (23.1% vs 23.6%), churn is 0.8% a month and NRR is 112%. Enterprise: 0.2% churn, NRR 118%. SMB: Inkwell's $9 plan has cut Palisade's win rate from 51% to 38%.

3. The CFO's $10.3M is really ~$4.2M, and the extra $1.2M over our plan depends on SMB. Contracts not renewing in 2027 and the 7% enterprise cap cut it to $7.6M; churn cuts it to $4.2M. Our plan gives $3.0M. If customers are more price-sensitive than we assume, both give ~$2.0M, so the flat 12% buys upside only if Inkwell has not changed SMB behaviour.

4. Raise in January, gate SMB on a test, and plan for new customers to close the 15% gap. ARR reaches ~$97.0M (+12.8%) before new customers; NRR stays ~113%. Mid-market and enterprise rises start at January renewals. An SMB test runs in Q1–Q2, with an H2 rise only if it passes. Churn triggers can pause any step.

slides.title: Appendix A1: Net gain = renewing ARR × retention × (price rise − churn caused by the rise), calibrated on the 2023 and 2024 price evidence

claims.claim: Net gain per segment = R × g × [p − c × (1 + p)]
evidence: R = ARR renewing in 2027: SMB 100% of $21.0M; mid-market 85% of $41.0M = $34.85M; enterprise 40% of $24.0M = $9.6M
g = share retained over 12 months at the H1 2026 monthly churn rate, (1 − m)^12
p = price rise; enterprise capped portion (60%) limited to 7%
c = extra share of retained ARR lost because of the rise; break-even when c = p/(1+p)

claims.claim: Sensitivity (c per point of price)
evidence: SMB 0.45%: 2023 +8% added 0.5pp churn for 6 months and 0.1pp for the next 6 = 3.6% ÷ 8
Mid-market and enterprise 0.21%: 2024 test conversion 23.1% vs 23.6% = 2.1% relative ÷ 10
Promo cohort: SMB × 2.9 (52% ÷ 18% citing price)
Downside: mid-market and enterprise at SMB sensitivity; core SMB ×2; promo ×1.5

normalized.recommendation: Raise prices in 2027 by segment: +10% for mid-market and enterprise from January 2027 renewals (enterprise capped contracts at +7%; multi-year contracts on their own terms), hold SMB list prices in H1 and approve the +8% test (July rollout decided at end of Q2 against the slide 13 gates), exclude the promo cohort from any rise and stop 50%-off offers (fund activation outreach), and close the 15% gap and fix the metrics (Sales to commit a plan for ≥$1.9M of net new-customer ARR; Finance to restate the board churn metric by segment and cohort).

alternatives_considered.treatment: CFO claim 'half right'; CS claim 'not credible': halving means 1.55%, below the 2.1% of normally onboarded customers; full activation worth ~$0.3M ARR in 2027.

assumptions_and_uncertainties: Mid-market renewals react like the +10% new sign-up test; the test covered new sign-ups over three months and renewal reaction is untested. At 2× (SMB-level) sensitivity, gain falls from $2.4M to $1.6M.
Core SMB price sensitivity since Inkwell is unknown — the main uncertainty in the pack; a rise could cost money and new customers.
Promo cohort cannot be won back with activation alone (activation explains ~30% of its excess churn); upside only, not counted.
Trailing NRR by segment repeats in 2027 (SMB 94%, mid-market 112%, enterprise 118%), giving +$8.0M — the biggest assumption in the bridge; each point of overall NRR ≈ $0.9M of exit ARR.
New-customer ARR of ≥$1.9M net by Dec 2027 is not in the pack; the pack has no pipeline data, so Sales must confirm.
Capped share of enterprise ARR (60%) assumed the same in the 2027 renewals; ±$0.1M, immaterial.
Board metric '1.4% → 2.3%' cannot be reconciled; the board may be misreading the trend.
Promo-cohort churn is derived using mid-2026 customer counts for H1 rates, so treat it as approximate.
Mid-market churn is slightly up (0.6% → 0.8%) and the pack does not explain it.
All repricing measured as a December 2027 run-rate, regardless of renewal month; this overstates revenue booked within 2027.
Effect of the price rise on new-customer conversion not modelled (no SMB data).
Downside case: mid-market and enterprise as price-sensitive as SMB was in 2023, core SMB twice as sensitive, promo cohort 1.5× its base.
Prepared from the 2026 briefing pack only (synthetic benchmark data).
